title: Invocation conductor: result propagation and cycle breakers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Multi-tool and function-call flows in the Core API can create accidental recursion, duplicate side-effects, and streaming inconsistencies when tool results are injected back into subsequent calls. This ticket implements an 'invocation conductor' that centralizes multi-tool chaining, enforces injection contracts for structured outputs, and provides multiple recursion/cycle breakers to avoid liveness and safety failures.

Goals:
- Define a deterministic protocol for tool result injection so that structured outputs are validated and sanitized before being re-consumed.
- Implement recursion guards (depth limit, token sentinel, idempotency keys, and provenance fencing) to stop accidental or malicious loops.
- Ensure streaming remains efficient: partial tool outputs can be surfaced while still guaranteeing final injection is atomic and consistent.
- Provide compatibility layers for existing SDKs and older API clients, minimizing breaking changes.

Scope of work:
1) Design an Invocation Conductor service that sits between the request router and tool runners. It will: provenance-tag tool outputs, apply injection transforms, validate against declared structured schemas, and maintain a short-lived invocation graph for loop detection.
2) Add three complementary loop guards: static depth limit (configurable per route), runtime provenance sentinel (unique run IDs + hop counters), and idempotency key enforcement for tools with side effects.
3) Streaming behavior: enable tools to stream partial chunks to clients immediately while buffering the final canonical payload for injection. Provide an explicit 'finalize' handshake that marks the canonical payload as commit-ready.
4) Compatibility: expose a feature-flagged compat API that accepts the legacy tool result envelope and upgrades it to the new conductor protocol server-side to avoid SDK churn. Document behavior differences for older SDK versions.
5) Observability and safety: emit invocation graph traces, guard-trigger metrics, and per-tool sanitized payload samples (PII redacted) to the Console. Add alerts for repeated guard triggers and high loop churn.

Acceptance criteria summary is below and detailed test cases are attached as comments.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor correctly validates and rejects tool injections that fail structured schema validation with a 422-style error and explanatory reason.
Three loop guards detect and stop recursion in injected flows during unit and integration tests: depth, provenance hop threshold, and idempotency collisions.
Streaming clients receive partial tool outputs immediately and final canonical injection only after 'finalize' handshake succeeds; no partial-injected state is visible to downstream tools.
Backward compatibility mode upgrades legacy envelopes and logs a compatibility audit event; no customer SDK changes required for opt-in rollout.
Telemetry for guard triggers, avg injection validation latency, and dropped cycles are visible in the Console dashboards and tied to runtime-1.24 release.
End-to-end integration tests for commonly used tool chains (search->rank->formatter, db-write->confirm) pass under typical load and simulated failure conditions.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes posted to Drive (link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/INVOCATION-CONDUCTOR) with initial sequence diagrams. We agreed on a conductor abstraction over direct tool-to-tool calls to centralize provenance.

2026-03-04 - Liam Chen: Prototype of the provenance header implemented in the local dev branch. It stains through existing grpc headers as X-Invoc-Path. Early tests show hop counting works across two chained tools. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128

2026-03-05 - Design review (Maya Rodriguez): Requested clearer UX for streaming vs injection semantics; suggested a short glossary table in the API docs to avoid confusion for SDK consumers. Added design doc link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Invocation+Conductor+Design
2026-03-07 - Security (Omar Haddad): Flagged that idempotency keys must not be guessable; recommended HMAC-based derivation using route secrets. Marked ticket for security review (required).

2026-03-09 - QA (Priya Singh): Provided test matrix for recursion scenarios including: mutual tool calls (A->B->A), long-cycle through 5 tools, and spoofed provenance headers. Will run once conductor integration is merged to staging. Test plan attached in Drive.

2026-03-11 - Liam Chen: Implemented 'finalize' handshake and streaming buffer. Set default conductor depth limit to 8 hops; added per-route override. Added feature flag runtime.conductor.v1 to gate rollout. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4192

2026-03-12 - PM (Eleanor Brooks): Confirmed rollout strategy: enable conductor.v1 for 10% of traffic on staging, run for 48h, escalate to 50% and run Canary daily checks for guard triggers. If any high-severity guard triggers spike, rollback.
notes:
Trade-offs considered: conservative default depth to avoid false positives vs developer pain for legitimate long pipelines; we prefer allowing per-route overrides and clear telemetry rather than increasing default limits. We also make the 'finalize' handshake mandatory for any tool that declares its output as 'injectable'. This prevents partial or malformed injections from creating inconsistent state.

Follow-ups: implement a lightweight visualizer in Console for invocation graphs (separate ticket), and a developer CLI lint that warns when tool definitions claim injectability without schema.
